analysis:
Scope. The packet records no drafted draw-rule text for the Special Draw Right under any alternative. Each rule below joins the alternative's recorded general rule to the right's recorded terms; the join and every causal reading are my interpretation, not graph proof or a record. The packet does not define 'versions', so I take them as the open forms of the decision: revocable (the working design) or permanent, with the training condition kept or dropped. The Book owner matched the three questions to revision 3 by identity; I rely on that matching and do not treat it as an author assertion.

Under A (not chosen). Recorded: draw is decoupled from hands; care is counted and nothing is owed. Derived: the skill claim keys draw to a capacity that A decouples, and the training condition keys draw to an act of return that A does not owe. The right stands under A only if the claim is read as counted care and the condition is dropped or recast as care. Neither reading is recorded.

Under B (not chosen). Recorded: hands are owed in proportion to draw; inside the window a shortfall is a deficit to repay, not a cut; the rule has a sunset. Derived: a claim on draw without owed hands is an exemption from the proportional rule, as the packet's significance reads it. A right that ends with the window fits; a permanent one outlasts the sunset, and the record says nothing about the rule after it. The training condition could be the repayment that squares the claim with B.

Under C (not chosen). Recorded: normal seasons follow A; a ratified Balance Stones threshold activates B's rule for a fixed window. Derived: the right's rule depends on the season. In normal seasons it is A's rule, so A's tension recurs under C. This weakens the packet's counterevidence that the tension may not arise if B or C is chosen. The record does not say whether the right is suspended, kept or re-ratified at activation.

Versions against failure modes. The recorded failure modes do not name the right, so each check is interpretive.
A: correlated shock: a revocable form gives the Council a withdrawal path if it holds that power; a permanent form has none. Lowland draw unhanded: no connection recorded. Surveillance of the tally: only condition-kept forms add apprentice records.
B: standing power through schedule: the Council holds the Hollow Gate schedule until Book 22 and the working design makes it the revoking body, so revocation sits with a schedule-holder; a permanent form adds standing beyond the window. Custody under another name: a permanent claim held by a lineage is closest to the recorded risk that knowledge hardens into hereditary privilege.
C: threshold as authority, unchecked activation, calm-year ratification failure, disputed gauge: none is connected to the right in the record. In calm years the right defaults to A's rule.

Summary (interpretive). The revocable form fits the most checks, and only if its terms are drafted for each regime. No form fits A without the counted-care reading. Under B only a form that ends with the window fits the sunset. Under C the right needs terms for both regimes. Revocability carries most of the fit, and the body that holds it is itself a failure mode. On the reader side, a permanent lineage claim under B would read as an exemption from the rule that cuts draw for hands not returned, a point the record does not resolve.

Links. The right reaches the alternatives only through shared nodes: it links to eng_ledger; A and B both link to th_hands_and_draw; the Book 20 conversion links th_hands_and_draw and eng_ledger. That is a recorded point of contact, not a recorded dependency. Book 24 records decisions on three questions, which does not show they are causally linked. That revocability and the finale are one decision is the packet's hypothesis. A also contradicts the Book 20 conversion as recorded, so A would require revisiting q-conversion-settlement, which the record already lists as open.

Left to the author: the finale (A, B, C or a third); the right's form and training condition; whether the Book 20 conversion is lasting; and whether the right belongs in C's ratified package. Named gaps: no earlier wording exists for the three questions, and six positional names are untied to any selected question. Neither is filled in.

recorded_observations.claim: Working wording: whether the lineage Special Draw Right is revocable or permanent, what training condition it carries, and who carries the Turn when the maintenance lineages end, not decided. The Book owner matched this question to revision 3 by identity; no earlier wording is recorded.

From Book 20 the maintenance lineages hold a Special Draw Right, conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage. The working design is revocable by the Council; whether it stays revocable is recorded as open.
The Special Draw Right gives skill a claim on draw, linking the maintenance lineages to the Ledger engine.

Finale Alternative A, recorded as not chosen: draw is decoupled from hands; care is counted and nothing is owed. Recorded failure modes: correlated shock, lowland draw left unhanded, and surveillance of the tally.

Finale Alternative B, recorded as not chosen: hands are owed in proportion to draw, and inside the window a shortfall is a deficit to repay, not a cut. It has a sunset. Recorded failure modes: standing power through schedule, and the Hall's custody returning under another name.

Finale Alternative C, recorded as not chosen: normal seasons follow A, and a ratified Balance Stones threshold activates B's rule for a fixed window. Recorded failure modes: the threshold becomes an authority, activation by the Reading Hall's reading may be unchecked, ratification fails in calm years, and the gauge is disputed.

Until Book 19 draw follows shares alone; from Book 20 it partly follows hands owed. Whether that conversion is a lasting settlement or a stage the finale must revisit is recorded as open (q-conversion-settlement).
Recorded risk: the maintenance lineages hold the knowledge needed to read the stones, and that knowledge may harden into hereditary privilege.

hypotheses.title: Revocability decides how far the right fits
hypotheses.description: The difference that matters is the right's term, not its existence. A revocable form can be drawn to end with B's window or C's ratified trigger, so the skill claim need not contradict a finale. A permanent form cannot be squared with B's sunset without a rule the record does not contain. Counter-reading: the packet records no revocation rule tied to any alternative, and the Council that would revoke also holds the schedule, so the lever may itself be the failure mode. Interpretive, not recorded; the author decides the form.

hypotheses.title: The training condition is the hinge
hypotheses.description: On this reading the skill claim is less contentious than the training condition, because the condition is the only element that ties draw to an act of return. Under A it must be dropped or recast as counted care, which would leave the skill claim standing on its own. Under B the condition could serve as the repayment that squares a claim with the owed-hands rule. If so, the choice of condition, not revocability, may decide which alternative the right can carry. Interpretive; the record does not say which reading the author intends.

hypotheses.title: C brings A's tension back in normal seasons
hypotheses.description: Under C the right would be governed by A's rule in normal seasons and by B's only inside the window. On this reading the claim meets A's tension most of the time, and C does not remove it. A reading that keeps the right clear of the tension would need an explicit term for normal seasons that the record does not contain. The finale would then have to state two rules for one right.

uncertainties: The packet does not define 'versions'. I took them as revocable or permanent, with the training condition kept or dropped; other drafted wordings would need their own check.
No draft draw-rule text for the right exists in the packet under any alternative. All three rules are derived from recorded general rules and the right's recorded terms.
Whether the lineage right exempts its holders from the Book 20 hands-to-draw conversion is not recorded.
What governs draw after B's sunset, and whether a permanent right would be squared with any rule then, is not recorded.
Whether the right is suspended, kept or re-ratified when C's threshold activates is not recorded, and neither is whether it belongs in C's ratified package.
Whether the Gate Table (Book 22) would change which body can revoke the right is not recorded.
Whether the training condition adds apprentice records to the tally is an inference from the condition's wording, not a recorded consequence.
Six positional names in these Books' prose stay untied to any selected question and are not used as references to the right.
